answer.decision: Regional token buckets with bounded global quotas and local burst allowance.
answer.action: Deploy one highly available limiter per region, using replicated tenant entitlements to assign bounded regional shares of each tenant’s global quota. Configure token-bucket capacity to absorb typical bursts of approximately 4× the five-minute-average rate for at least 20 seconds. During partitions, continue regional enforcement within the assigned share and burst ceiling; rebalance regional shares after connectivity returns.
reasons: Per-tenant regional enforcement prevents the small cohort of high-volume tenants from exhausting shared capacity.
Local burst capacity reduces costly false throttling during observed short traffic spikes.
Keeping synchronous cross-region coordination out of the request path avoids the measured 180 ms p99 control-plane latency.
Bounded regional quota shares permit continued requests during partitions while limiting aggregate quota overshoot.
Regionally replicated entitlement data supplies quota inputs without requiring a global lookup.
The architecture requires at most one new type of stateful dependency and is more suitable for a five-person platform team than a globally coordinated design.
A centralized global limiter would add latency and create a cross-region availability dependency, while uncoordinated per-instance buckets cannot reliably enforce tenant-wide quotas.
assumptions: Tenant global quotas can be divided among regions and periodically rebalanced according to demand.
A small and explicitly bounded quota overshoot during partitions is acceptable.
A regional limiter cluster is counted as one new stateful dependency type despite deployment in three regions.
Tenant-specific burst settings may be tuned when the observed 4× pattern is not representative.
risks: Fixed regional quota shares can falsely throttle traffic concentrated in one region while another region has unused allocation.
Concurrent regional enforcement during a partition can produce bounded global quota overshoot.
Generous burst capacity can increase pressure on shared infrastructure if many large tenants burst simultaneously.
Limiter outages require a predefined, bounded fallback policy; unrestricted fail-open risks capacity exhaustion, while fail-closed risks a regional outage.
Quota allocation, rebalancing, and partition recovery require careful observability and operational procedures.

citations.claim: The top 2 percent of tenants generate 61 percent of peak request volume, supporting tenant-level isolation.
Bursts frequently reach 4 times a tenant's five-minute average for less than 20 seconds, supporting local burst capacity.
Cross-region control-plane round trips have 180 ms p99 latency, arguing against synchronous global enforcement.
An 11-minute regional dependency outage occurred while regional application instances remained healthy, supporting partition-tolerant regional enforcement.
The platform team has capacity for at most one new stateful dependency.
Tenant entitlement data is already replicated regionally and can supply per-tenant quota inputs without a new global lookup.
